title: Local cyclotomic group algebras are products of full matrix algebras
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ and let $G$ be a finite group with $g^N=1$ for every $g\in G$. Fix a primitive complex $N$th root of unity $\zeta_N$, put $A=\mathbf Z[1/N,\zeta_N]$, and let $\Lambda=A_{\mathfrak p}$ for a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Define the group algebra $\Lambda[G]$ to be the free $\Lambda$-module on symbols $[g]$, with multiplication $[g][h]=[gh]$ extended bilinearly. There are an integer $r\geq1$, integers $d_1,\ldots,d_r\geq1$, and a $\Lambda$-algebra isomorphism
$$\Lambda[G]\cong\prod_{i=1}^{r}M_{d_i}(\Lambda).$$
Here $M_d(\Lambda)$ is the ring of $d$ by $d$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] with the usual matrix addition and multiplication.

proof.text: Put $m=|G|\geq1$. Every prime $q$ dividing $m$ divides $N$. To see this, realize $G$ by field automorphisms: let $L=\mathbf Q(x_g:g\in G)$ be the field of rational functions in independent variables indexed by $G$, a field extension of $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-field-extension]. For $h\in G$ the permutation $x_g\mapsto x_{hg}$ of the variables extends uniquely to a $\mathbf Q$-algebra automorphism $\sigma_h$ of the polynomial ring and then of its fraction field $L$, with inverse $\sigma_{h^{-1}}$; $\sigma_h\sigma_k=\sigma_{hk}$ on the variables, hence everywhere, and $\sigma_h(x_1)=x_h$, so $h\mapsto\sigma_h$ is an injective homomorphism. Its image $H$ is a finite subgroup of the $\mathbf Q$-algebra automorphisms of $L$ with $|H|=m$, isomorphic to $G$, so orders agree. By [lem-exc-finite-group-cauchy] applied to $H$, choose $g\in G$ of order $q$. Divide $N=aq+s$, $0\leq s<q$; then $g^s=g^N(g^q)^{-a}=1$, so minimality of the order forces $s=0$. Thus all prime factors of $m$ divide $N$, and for sufficiently large $e$ one has $N^e=mt$ with an integer $t$. Hence $t/N^e$ is an inverse of $m$ in $A$ and in $\Lambda$. This also covers $m=1$, with inverse $1$.

proof.text: By [lem-per-cyclotomic-local-ring-dvr], $\Lambda$ is a field or a DVR. It embeds in $\mathbf C$ by sending a fraction $a/s$ to the same quotient, since $A\subset\mathbf C$ is a domain and the denominators are nonzero. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$, also embedded in $\mathbf C$. It has characteristic zero, and $\zeta_N$ still has order exactly $N$. Apply [lem-per-cyclotomic-field-brauer-splitting] to obtain $\theta:K[G]\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^r M_{d_i}(K)$. The coordinate bases $[g]$ and $E^i_{ab}$ show that $\sum_i d_i^2=m$. If $\Lambda$ is a field, $K=\Lambda$ and this is the required conclusion. In what follows $\Lambda$ is a DVR.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, integral representation input. Agent-written local-order proof supplying the matrix decomposition, using the stated field-splitting and coefficient-ring inputs.

proof.text: Write $V_i=K^{d_i}$ and let $\rho_i(g)$ be the $i$th component of $\theta([g])$, acting on column vectors; these are invertible since $[g]^{-1}=[g^{-1}]$. Inside $V_i$ set $L_i=\sum_{g\in G}\rho_i(g)\Lambda^{d_i}$. It is generated by the finitely many vectors $\rho_i(g)e_a$, is $G$-stable by reindexing $g\mapsto hg$, contains $\Lambda^{d_i}$ by $g=1$, and is torsion-free because it lies in a vector space over the fraction field. By [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free], choose a finite $\Lambda$-basis of $L_i$. This basis is a $K$-basis of $V_i$: it spans since $e_a\in L_i$, and a $K$-linear relation can be multiplied by the product of its nonzero denominators to become a $\Lambda$-linear relation. Thus it has exactly $d_i$ elements.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, integral representation input. Agent-written local-order proof supplying the matrix decomposition, using the stated field-splitting and coefficient-ring inputs.

proof.text: The actions on $L_i$ define the $\Lambda$-algebra homomorphism $f:\Lambda[G]\to B=\prod_i\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(L_i)\cong\prod_i M_{d_i}(\Lambda)$. Let $C_i\in\operatorname{GL}_{d_i}(K)$ have the chosen basis vectors of $L_i$ as columns. On extending scalars, $f_K$ sends $x$ to $(C_i^{-1}\theta(x)_i C_i)_i$, and hence is an isomorphism. Both sides of $f$ have bases of size $m$, namely $[g]$ and the matrix units. Let $M$ be its $m$ by $m$ coordinate matrix, with columns $f([g])$. Its determinant is nonzero in $K$; surjectivity over $\Lambda$ will be checked integrally.

proof.text: For any finite free algebra $D$ write $t_D(x)$ for the sum of diagonal entries of the matrix of left multiplication by $x$. Over $K$ this sum is unchanged by conjugation: $\sum_a(UV)_{aa}=\sum_{a,b}U_{ab}V_{ba}=\sum_b(VU)_{bb}$. Consequently $t_B(f(x)f(y))=t_{\Lambda[G]}(xy)$, since the left multiplication matrices become conjugate by $f_K$ over $K$, and $\Lambda\hookrightarrow K$ is injective. On the group basis the latter pairing has matrix $H_{g,h}=m$ if $gh=1$ and $0$ otherwise: left translation by $gh\neq1$ has no fixed basis vector. Thus $\det H=\pm m^m$ is a unit. In the matrix-unit basis of $B$, put $T_{u,v}=t_B(uv)\in\Lambda$; this is an integral matrix since multiplication in $B$ has integral structure constants. Bilinearity gives $H=M^{\mathsf T}TM$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, integral representation input. Agent-written local-order proof supplying the matrix decomposition, using the stated field-splitting and coefficient-ring inputs.

proof.text: Taking determinants gives $\pm m^m=\det(M)^2\det(T)$. As $m$ is a unit by Step 1, this identity gives an explicit inverse of $\det(M)$: multiply $\det(M)\det(T)$ by $(\pm m^m)^{-1}$. The adjugate identity [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] now gives the two-sided inverse $\det(M)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(M)$ with entries in $\Lambda$. Therefore $f$ is a bijective $\Lambda$-linear map, as well as a unital multiplicative map. Its inverse preserves multiplication, the unit and scalars by applying the injective map $f$ to the respective identities. This is the required $\Lambda$-algebra isomorphism, with the positive $r,d_i$ already supplied by Step 2.
